reason: Attempt 8 fell to 74.6%, especially confusing prepaid accounts with deposit accounts and vehicle financing with personal loans. Replace its rigid category order with direct contextual distinctions for those errors and the unchanged ten-label vocabulary.
instruction: Choose the one product category that best explains the consumer's relationship with the respondent. Use Mortgage for financing secured by a home; Student loan for education borrowing; Vehicle loan or lease for purchasing, financing, leasing, paying for, or repossessing a car or other vehicle. Use Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan for non-education personal/installment borrowing, payday loans, cash advances, or cash borrowed against the title of an already-owned vehicle; do not call ordinary vehicle-purchase financing a personal or title loan merely because the narrative says loan. Use Credit card for a revolving card account and its purchase disputes, billing, interest, balance transfers, or rewards. Use Prepaid card for a stored-value, gift, reloadable, payroll, unemployment, tax-refund, or benefits-disbursement card and access to its balance; receiving a deposit or having an account number does not by itself turn such a card into a checking account. Use Checking or savings account for an ordinary bank deposit relationship and its balance, access, fees, checks, or debit-card servicing. Use Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service when the disputed relationship is a remittance, wire, payment-processing, electronic-transfer, wallet, or virtual-currency service. Use Debt collection when the respondent pursues or reports a collection debt. Use Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports when the respondent provides a credit bureau or consumer-reporting service. A secondary reference to another product, a payment destination, a statute, or a requested remedy does not override the main relationship.
